items.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: No, there was an alto saxophone player named Bobby Plater. He was the lead alto player.

ctx.x: [Laughs] Who was the straw boss for the band? I guess, Gladys.

No, there was an alto saxophone player named Bobby Plater. He was the lead alto player. When you say “straw boss,” that’s the one who stomps off the tempo when the bandleader isn’t on the stand. Usually, it’s traditional for the bandleader to not be on the stand if you’re playing say a dance date. The band usually plays two or three numbers to so-called warm up, and then here comes the maestro. The audience says, “Ahhhhhh!”
